title: Linear Momentum

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Laws of Motion

explanation: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity, and it's a vector quantity pointing in the same direction as the velocity. In an isolated system (no net external force), total momentum is conserved — this principle underlies the analysis of collisions and explosions, even when kinetic energy is not conserved (as in inelastic collisions).

workedExample.scenario: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s.

commonMistakes: Treating momentum as conserved for an individual object when external forces act on it — conservation applies to the TOTAL momentum of an isolated system.
Confusing momentum conservation with kinetic energy conservation — momentum is conserved in ALL collisions (elastic and inelastic); kinetic energy is only conserved in elastic collisions.
genZNote: Momentum conservation is the one law that still holds even when energy 'goes missing' into heat/sound during a crash.
